args.question: ok this looks rough, I'm way behind on count. Of my options (g2, b6, a7, b7, b8, c8) which one actually gives me the best shot at winning by the end? I don't have time to work out all the flips myself.

parts.content:
Play **b7**.

Why: in this endgame it’s the best shot because it manages the **bottom-left corner fight** without immediately giving White an easy corner/edge sequence. The flashier edge moves like **a7/b8/c8** can let White control the empty **a8** corner area afterward. **b7** is the tempo move that keeps Black’s final count best.

args.question: honestly still not 100% sure why white passing that one turn was such a big deal - like why couldn't they just take g2 or h1 right then instead of being stuck? can you explain that in plain terms?

parts.content:
Because in Othello you **can’t choose any empty square** — you can only play a square if it **flips at least one disc**.

So White couldn’t just take **g2** or **h1** unless placing there would sandwich a line of Black discs between that new White disc and another White disc.

A **pass** means: White had **zero legal flips anywhere**, so they were forced to skip. That’s huge in the endgame because Black effectively gets the next tempo — you got to choose the order of the last few squares, and that can swing corners/last flips by a lot.

Plain version: White wasn’t “stuck strategically”; they were **stuck by the rules**. No flip = no move.

That makes sense now — so it wasn't some fancy strategy, White literally had no legal spot to place a disc. Good to know for next time. Thanks for walking me through this whole thing, final score held at 33-31, so I'll take the win!
